bull.b: Completing pivotal DME enrollment ahead of schedule reduces execution risk and keeps EyePoint on track for 2027 data. It also supports potential expansion of DURAVYU beyond wet AMD into a large retinal disease market.

A meaningful reduction in injection burden could differentiate DURAVYU in retinal care, where treatment frequency affects adherence and clinic workload. This benefit may support adoption even though the full primary endpoint was not met.

The stated cash runway extends through key Phase 3 milestones, giving EyePoint time to generate clinical evidence without an immediate financing requirement. This provides strategic flexibility while its pipeline approaches potential commercialization.

bear.b: Failure to meet the primary endpoint in the full wet AMD dataset increases regulatory and approval uncertainty for DURAVYU. It may also require reliance on LUCIA and additional evidence, delaying or weakening the path to commercialization.

The sharp revenue decline demonstrates that EyePoint currently lacks a dependable commercial revenue base, with results affected by deferred-license revenue recognition. This leaves the company highly dependent on pipeline success and future partnerships.

Persistent operating and free-cash-flow losses consume the balance sheet while Phase 3 development and manufacturing investment continue. Even with modest debt, sustained burn raises future financing, dilution and execution risks.
